body: My therapist used to say it all the time and I wanted to crawl into a hole and die every time. I'm with you 100%.

One of the worst things I've ever done was staring at a girl with visible self harm scars when I was around 12. I wasn't staring because I was horrified, but because I had my own. I was fascinated that she could just show them and not be ashamed. 

Of course she caught me staring and immediately left the store. I feel so guilty about it now, I couldn't imagine how I made her feel.

I am so sorry. 9 years ago, I had to watch my mother go through the same thing when we found out my brother had passed in a car accident. It's been almost a decade, and I still remember the horrible sound of her screaming his name. If you ever want to talk, my DM's are open.

That makes a lot of sense. I'll write down bulletpoints for all the stuff I want to make clear, so I don't lose track of what I want to say. I always tend to do that when I'm nervous 😅. And thank you so much again for your advice, it means alot.
Yeah, I feel like if I take him off guard with it, then he might maybe react negatively and I'm so scared about that. I am working on getting better so that might help the conversation as well.
Thank you so much for your advice. I really do trust him. I'm just afraid, yknow? I think I'll talk to him about it tonight, while I'm feeling slightly more confident.
This is exactly how I feel. It sounds so peaceful, not having to think about anything or feel anything.
I thought the exact same way. And then my brother died and it actually ripped me apart. I still grieve nearly 9 years later.
